report:
Reviewed the complete kind_wrappers claim, its single ordinary implementation association in symbol/mod.rs, both associated tests, and captured model/database setup context. Requirements are heterogeneous Symbol membership/results, kind-specific operation receivers, identity-preserving erasure, correct-kind recovery, and rejection of incorrect-kind recovery. The macro creates one private local discriminant per represented kind plus an external interned handle, and public SymbolData variants for kind-aware matching. From implementations move the exact local or external handle into Symbol without allocating a new definition; data() reconstructs the corresponding wrapper using the local discriminant or external kind. Module and enum item interfaces return heterogeneous Symbol slices, while FnSymbol::sig, TraitSymbol::sig/items, EnumSymbol::variants and ModSymbol::expanded_module_items have kind-specific receivers. Their semantic producer algorithms are outside this conversion claim. module(), trait_symbol(), and external_adt() discriminate recovered variants and reject represented mismatches with None. Local-only intrinsic and macro-invocation kinds remain local payload variants. Raw unsupported external kinds reaching the existing todo branch are not represented kind wrappers; this review does not certify support for them or arbitrary forged external wrapper payloads.

The review discovered and reproduced an actual represented-kind error: UseSymbol declared Ext(SymExtKind::Mod), so an external use could not recover via SymbolData. Added the anchor-associated external_use_roundtrip_preserves_kind_and_identity regression and ran cargo test -p sage-ir --test kind_wrappers external_use_roundtrip_preserves_kind_and_identity before the fix: 0 passed, 1 failed, with panic at symbol/mod.rs:331 'not yet implemented: NDM: add all variants here'. The intended result is the same UseSymbol wrapper and rejection as module/trait. Corrected only the UseSymbol external discriminant to SymExtKind::Use, formatted with cargo fmt, and reran the same command: 1 passed, 0 failed. The ordinary regression visibly asserts Symbol identity equals conversion of the original external handle, exact UseSymbol recovery, equality of the recovered wrapper, and None for both wrong-kind module and trait recovery. It would catch the original missing dispatch and accidental conflation with modules.

The second associated entry sage_meta::todo::symbols_kind_wrappers remains explicitly deferred. Its empty body is not behavioral evidence. Its stated prerequisite is complete compile-time/API conversion and local/external dispatch coverage for every supported symbol kind; that requires a per-kind fixture and conversion/rejection matrix and compile-time interface checks. The focused external-use regression does not discharge that broader work, including the local-kind and other external-kind matrices or uniform semantic dispatcher coverage. This is a justified retained test TODO, not a claim that complete test adequacy has been achieved. Existing abstract modeled interfaces likewise are not executable dispatcher tests. No TODO is upgraded or removed. Source inspection supports the current represented-kind conversion mechanism after the minimal fix; test coverage remains honestly partial under its explicit TODO. Fresh start after changes captured the complete current evidence. The focused regression and formatting were executed by this reviewer; broader workspace tests/build and mandatory independent quality reviews are coordinated by root, and no results for them are claimed here.
